data.name: Emerentina
data.gender_notes: Emerentina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin 'emerare', to shine or be radiant. In the early Christian tradition, Emerentina was the name of a martyr who was said to have shone with the light of her faith even during her suffering. Her name is associated with the precious stone emerald, representing eternal beauty and renewal. The name Emerentina carries the meaning “Emerald, ever-radiant” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Emerentina usually hope their child will grow to embody emerald, ever-radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Emerentina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Emerald, ever-radiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Emerentina total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: עמרטינה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עמרטינה היא שם נשא עמר, אשר נמצא בקשר לעמודה התשיעית בלוח האבדים. שם זה יכול להאזכר את השלמות והאומץ של חיים שבטוחים. על פי המסורת, עמרטינה היא שם של אחותו של הנביא בכירה, שהתגלה על ידי האל כסמל לקדושת האשה. שם זה יכול לבטא את החשיבות הרבה של האישה בחברה הנוצרית.

in_greek.name: Εμερετίνα
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο όρος Εμερετίνα προέρχεται από το ονοματεπώνυμο Αμερ, που σχετίζεται με την εννέατη στήλη του αβγάντη. Ο όρος μπορεί να αναφέρεται στην ολοτελεία και την αμεσητότητα της ζωής που είναι ασφαλής. Σύμφωνα με τη παράδοση, η Εμερετίνα ήταν το όνομα της αδερφής του προφήτη Βηρίου, που αποκαλύφθηκε από τον Θεό ως σύμβολο της αγιοσύνη της γυναίκας. Ο όρος μπορεί να εκφράσει την μεγάλη αξία της γυναίκας στην χριστιανική κοινωνία.

in_latin.name: Emerentina
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Emerentina derivatur a nomine Amor, quod est connexio novena columna Abgad. Nomen hoc potest referre ad perfectam et firmam vitam. Secundum traditionem, Emerentina fuit nomen sororis prophetae Birei, qui apparuerat a Deo ut significare sanctitatem mulieris. Nomen hoc potest exprimere gravitatem mulieris in communitate christiana.

in_english.name: Emerentina
in_english.meaning: daughter of the name Amor, symbolizing love and devotion
in_english.long_meaning: Emerentina is a name derived from the Hebrew root Amor, connected to the ninth letter of the Abjad alphabet. The name represents a person with a steadfast and complete life. According to tradition, Emerentina was the name of the sister of the prophet Berechiah, revealed by God as a symbol of the holiness of women. The name signifies the importance and value of women in Christian society, reflecting their role as caregivers, nurturers, and guardians of faith.

data.cultural_impact: Emerentina is a beautiful, classic name with a rich history. Its Latin origins add an air of sophistication and elegance, while its association with a martyr adds a touch of courage and strength. In some parts of Europe, the name has been popular for centuries, and it continues to be used today in both the Catholic and Orthodox Christian traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: Emerentina is a name that inspires us to shine with the light of our faith. It reminds us that even in the darkest of times, we can be radiant and beautiful, just like the emerald stone that represents eternal beauty and renewal. The name is a call to live our lives with dignity, strength, and courage, and to let our light shine for all to see. It is a reminder to trust in the power of God to uplift us even in the most challenging moments of our lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Emerentia: Patroness of eternal rest and quiet repose, symbolizing the tranquility and peace that comes with the end of earthly struggles and the beginning of eternal life. Her name inspires contemplation of the transient nature of earthly existence and the eternal rewards of faith.

historical_references.reference: According to tradition, Emerentina was the name of a noble Roman virgin who, during the Diocletian persecution, was martyred for her faith. She is said to have been imprisoned and a leaden barrel and rolled down the Palatine Hill, then thrown into the Tiber River. Her relics were later discovered in the Church of San Lorenzo in Damaso in Rome, and she was venerated as a saint.
historical_references.context: Christian martyrdom during the Diocletian persecution of Christians

historical_references.reference: The name Emerentia or Emerentina was also given to a number of early Christian saints, including a virgin and martyr in Africa who was tortured and beheaded during the persecutions of the Emperor Valerian. Her feast day is celebrated on February 17.
historical_references.context: Christian martyrdom during the Valerian persecution of Christians

modern_usage.modern_context: The Christian name 'Emerentina' is most commonly associated with Saint Emerentiana, a martyr from ancient Rome. In modern contexts, her name is revered in Roman Catholicism, particularly through various platforms. On Catholic websites and apps, Saint Emerentiana is the subject of numerous articles, prayers, and devotional resources. Social media, particularly among devout Catholics and spirituality enthusiasts, is another platform where her name is used in various ways, such as in hashtags, posts, and groups dedicated to her veneration. Lastly, devotional books and merchandise, such as prayer cards, rosaries, and statues, are popular ways for individuals to connect with her spirit and keep her memory alive.

name_in_real_life.story: Elizabeth Emerentina, a minister in Rome, Italy, shares that their name Emerentina meaning "Emerald, ever-radiant" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.
